correctness.rationale: A direct induced-P4 characterization is proved for every a,b>=1 and 0<=t<=min(a,b): any chordless four-path has its endpoints on a deleted matching pair and admits exactly the stated index patterns. Disjoint counting of overlap-free, one-side-singleton, and two-by-two matched configurations yields the full bivariate enumerator, including t=0 and size-one boundaries. The consecutive-t difference is factored exactly and interpreted as a nonnegative coefficient count, with its uv coefficient (a-1)(b-1)-2t controlling the unique equality case. For crowns n>=3, all one-vertex-maximal sets are classified by disjoint partitions, one-side singleton/full other side, and two matched pairs. The proof establishes every claimed cardinality and exception. The packaged adjacency-based program reproduces 169304 exhaustive subset tests across 129 profiles and 9282 arithmetic comparison checks; these finite checks do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The exact bivariate feasible-solution polynomial and all minimal-deletion multiplicities answer a natural graph-modification counting question on a three-parameter class, rather than a restricted numerical instance. Matching deletion does not generally preserve induced-P4-freeness, so the coefficientwise monotonicity result and unique equality case are a nontrivial structural property. The crown facet distribution exhibits unbounded forbidden sizes for inclusion-minimal cograph vertex-deletion solutions, with explicit mechanisms. No speculative application or inflated claim of an entirely new cograph concept is needed.
